t.1.154.1: Near Gaṅgādvāra there lived a great seer of mighty austerities, Bharadvāja, of great wisdom, ever rigorous in his vows.
t.1.154.3: Then, on the riverbank, the wind carried away her garment; seeing her with her clothing stripped away, the seer thereupon desired her.
t.1.154.2: Having gone to the Gaṅgā to bathe, the seer saw there the Apsaras Ghṛtācī, who had already arrived before him and was present there, bathing in the river.
t.1.154.5: Then a son, Droṇa, was born to that wise man. He studied the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas in their entirety.
t.1.154.4: As his mind became fixed upon her, the seer, who had been a celibate since his youth, was aroused and his semen spilled; he placed it in a wooden vessel.
t.1.154.6: Now Bharadvāja had a friend, a king named Pṛṣata; to him too a son was born at that time, named Drupada.
t.1.154.7: Going constantly to the hermitage, Pārṣata, that bull among kṣatriyas, played together with Droṇa and also pursued his studies with him.
t.1.154.8: Then, when Pṛṣata had passed away, Drupada became king. Droṇa, too, heard that Rāma was wishing to give away all his wealth.
t.1.154.9: But to Rāma, who had set out for the forest, the son of Bharadvāja said: "Know me to be Droṇa, who has come here desiring wealth, O bull among the twice-born."
t.1.154.10: Rāma said: Only this body of mine is left to me now. Brahman, choose one of the two, either my weapons or my body.
t.1.154.11: Droṇa said: Your honor should give me all the weapons, together with the means of withdrawing them, and the method of employing them all.
t.1.154.12: Saying "So be it," the scion of Bhṛgu then gave them to him; and Droṇa, having received them, felt that he had achieved his purpose.
t.1.154.13: And, his heart filled with joy, having obtained from Rāma the most highly esteemed Brahmāstra, he became superior among men.
t.1.154.14: Then the mighty Bhāradvāja, a tiger among men, approached Drupada and said, "Know me as your friend."
t.1.154.15: One who is not learned in the Veda is no friend to one learned in the Veda, one who is not a chariot-warrior is no friend to a chariot-warrior, and one who is not a king is no friend even to a king; why then do you cling to a former friendship?
t.1.154.17: To him, the wise Droṇa, who had arrived, Bhīṣma, bringing together his grandsons along with riches of many kinds, gave them over as pupils.
t.1.154.16: Having resolved in his mind concerning the Pāñcāla king, that wise one went to Nāgasāhvaya, the city of the foremost of the Kurus.
t.1.154.18: Then the learned Droṇa, having assembled all his disciples, spoke these words to them, intending it truly for the distress of Drupada.
t.1.154.19: A certain teacher's fee is turning over in my heart; it should be paid by you once you have mastered the weapons. Speak the truth about this, O sinless ones.
t.1.154.20: And when all the Pāṇḍavas had become skilled in weapons and had completed their diligent training, Droṇa then spoke these words once more, for the sake of his fee.
t.1.154.21: There is a king named Drupada, the son of Pṛṣata, lord of men in Chattravatī. Having wrested that kingdom from him, let it be given to me quickly.
t.1.154.22: Then the five sons of Pāṇḍu, having defeated Drupada in battle, bound him together with his ministers and presented him to Droṇa.
t.1.154.23: Once again, O lord of men, I seek friendship with you; for one who is not a king, it is said, cannot be the friend of a king.
t.1.154.25: That very great insult did not depart from the king's heart even for a moment; he became dejected and grew thin.
t.1.154.24: Therefore, Yajñasena, I have striven for your kingdom. You are king on the southern bank of the Bhāgīrathī, and I on the northern.
